title: Barnes's brothers and sister and their instruments
summary: He names his brothers Thomas, Freddie and Alfred, their ages and instruments, and a sister who played nothing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I wanted to ask some more about the plantation down there. We talked to Sonny Henry a couple weeks ago. He couldn't remember who else was in the band. He said you'd know all of those fellas. You told us about your three brothers and you. Yeah. Do you remember who else? Some of the men.
Whenever they get the brothers' names. I know all the men that are in there, but they're not living.
Well, if you know their names, then your names are your brothers too.
You want to know that too?
It would be nice to have them, yes.
Were they still living? Any of your brothers living?
No, they're all down. Thomas Bonds was the oldest. Freddie Bonds.
How much older was the oldest brother than you?
Just about three years different. Freddie Bonds was the second. Then Alfred Bonds. Then I had a sister. Well, she's older than I am. It was four boys and one girl. Did she play any instrument?
No, she didn't. Piano, guitar, nothing like that?
No, she wasn't. And I was the last. We were about three years apart. My oldest brother might have been about fifteen years, fourteen, fifteen years older than me, you know.
What instruments did they play that? Thomas played what?
And Freddie? Huh? And Freddie Bonds? Baritone.
